key_insight: A single monolithic lattice Boltzmann formulation can simulate both free-fluid and heterogeneous porous regions in one domain while correctly capturing porosity-scaled pressure, convection, and isotropic viscous stresses.
engineering_relevance: This enables efficient device-scale design and analysis of flows through engineered porous structures with spatially varying porosity, without stitching together separate solvers.
method: Standard-lattice LBM with one kinetic equation for free-fluid/porous interactions
Generalized forcing for Darcy-Forchheimer drag, variable porosity, and body forces
Brinkman-like effective viscous stress with tunable bulk viscosity and independent sound speed
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on 2D benchmark flow problems and shown to recover the intended hydrodynamic behavior in both porous and free-fluid regions.
watch_item: Accuracy and stability likely depend on careful parameterization of porosity, drag, and forcing terms, especially near sharp free-fluid/porous interfaces.
paper_title: Monolithic kinetic algorithm for heterogeneous porous media systems using a continuous one-domain approach
